$comment: How the tree is configured, built and tested, as CMake, an IDE and `omw` read it. A visible preset is
`<flavour>-<system>` and inherits the flavour, the system and `common`, in that order: the earlier one wins
a variable both set. Hidden presets are parts. Each flavour builds in `build-<flavour>`. Each visible
configure preset has a build preset and a workflow preset of its name, so `cmake --workflow --preset
debug-linux` configures, builds and tests a clone without `omw`, which builds through the same presets.
Version 10 is the first that takes a `$comment`.

configurePresets.name: common
$comment: Every flavour, each building every program, the tests and the benchmarks. ccache drives Clang and MSVC,
and the compile database is what an editor reads. The libraries are the vcpkg set `omw` names in
OMW_VCPKG_SET (`omw deps-set`, `pins.py`), built static, through its own toolchain file: host tools
and libraries share the system's one triplet, and the manifest is the set's to install, never a
configure's. Ninja is the pinned one `omw` names in OMW_NINJA. What the tree fetches is
`cmake/Dependencies.cmake`'s. Warnings are errors, by CMake's own switch, for the tree's targets
alone (`cmake/Checks.cmake`), and so are CMake's own dev and deprecation warnings, a configure's.

configurePresets.name: linux
configurePresets.$comment: The set's triplet; lld and thin archives are `cmake/Flags.cmake`'s, as every system's flags are.

configurePresets.name: windows
configurePresets.$comment: The set's triplet, whose libraries link MSVC's runtime statically, as every program does.

configurePresets.name: one-link
$comment: One link at a time, beside compiles at every core. A sanitized link of the game, the harness or
`openmw-tests` peaks at 4.5 GB of anonymous memory and 6.3 GB of mapped files under mold, and three
of them at once exhausted a 16 GB hosted runner, which then lost its connection to GitHub.

configurePresets.name: debug
configurePresets.$comment: Every assert: the everyday build, and what CI builds and tests on every system.

configurePresets.name: release
$comment: `-O3 -DNDEBUG` with line tables and frame pointers (`cmake/Flags.cmake`): the build a number is quoted
from and the archive is installed from. Link-time optimisation where OMW_LTO says `ON`, as a tagged
release does, and a desk that measures what ships.

configurePresets.name: asan
$comment: Debug under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, as upstream runs its tests. Linux
only: MSVC's sanitizer is unmeasured here. The options it needs are its test preset's. Warnings
are not errors here: GCC's manual recommends against `-Werror` with a sanitizer, whose
instrumentation gives the flow warnings false positives (GCC 16 reported libstdc++'s `std::regex`,
GCC 13 a one-element vector). Debug holds the same code to every warning.

configurePresets.name: tsan
$comment: Debug under ThreadSanitizer, which cannot share a build with AddressSanitizer: the races between the
threads the ray tracer keeps, the cell reader, the workers and the harness's instruments. Linux only,
as asan is, and with warnings that are not errors, for the same reason. The options it needs are its
test preset's.

testPresets.name: tests
$comment: Every test run: a failing test's output shown, and a build that registers no test is a failure.
Five minutes a suite, ten times the slowest one under the sanitizers: a test that hangs, as one
of `openmw-tests` does on Windows now and then, fails with the test it was in, where a job would
wait out its three hours and say nothing. The GPU suites state a limit of their own, which
`cmake/Tests.cmake` says why. Every suite runs in a new order each time, so a test
that leans on what an earlier one left fails at once: a test that captured stderr and never
gave it back broke every later death test in its binary, and ran in upstream's order for years.
The run prints its seed, and `GTEST_RANDOM_SEED` repeats it. A filter that matches no test is a
failure and not a pass, on a Google Test that reads `GTEST_FAIL_IF_NO_TEST_SELECTED`; an older
one ignores it.

testPresets.name: address-sanitizer
$comment: `protect_shadow_gap=0` is required: ASan's shadow gap covers part of what the NVIDIA driver maps,
and `vkCreateDevice` fails, which the RTX tests would read as a skip. The leak check is off,
because the driver, the loader, the layers and dbus hold heaps for the life of the process;
`ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1` from the environment turns it back on. A finding fails the run. `omw`
runs every asan program under these.

testPresets.name: thread-sanitizer
$comment: A race fails the run, as an AddressSanitizer finding does, and its report keeps the stack of the
other side's lock as well. `omw` runs every tsan program under these.
